proposal.thesis: UNH reported a ~30% Q2 2026 adjusted EPS beat ($6.38 vs $4.90 est.) on 2026-07-16 and raised FY26 adjusted EPS guidance to $19.50-$20.00 from prior '>$18.25', with $2B of buyback completed in Q2 toward a ~$2.5B 2026 program (SEC 8-K, sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000731766/000073176626000191/earningsrelease2q26_7152.htm). Price sits essentially at its 200-week moving average ($437.56 vs $435.38 close, -0.5%), a historically strong reversion zone for a quality mega-cap, with an unfilled post-earnings gap (+7.4%), ADX 45.3 confirming a newly-forming uptrend (DI+ 34.5 dominant), and RSI a non-overbought 62.7. Analyst consensus (mean target $437.81, +0.8% vs spot) has not yet caught up to the magnitude of the beat and raise, leaving room for estimate/target revisions over coming weeks. Demand driver is healthcare -- fully independent of the hyperscaler_server_capex bet (DELL/HPE) that produced this book's only two losses.
catalysts: Sell-side estimate and price-target revisions catching up to the raised FY26 guide over the next 2-3 weeks
Q3 2026 earnings, expected ~mid-October 2026 (~90 days out), the next hard confirm/deny on the margin-reset narrative
Continued 2026 buyback execution (~$2.5B program, $2B already completed in Q2) providing technical support on pullbacks
proposal.macro_context: Regime is supportive (SPY 7.7% above its 200-DMA, regime score 4/5) but rates are rising (10Y +23bp, 2Y +35bp over 3 months) and CPI is reaccelerating -- a headwind for richly-multiple growth names, which argues for a lower-beta (0.2), reasonably-valued (fwd P/E ~23.6x) mega-cap over a chase into an already-extended momentum name like CRWD or AMD today.
proposal.risk_map: UNH has a real history of medical-cost-ratio guidance shocks -- that is exactly what drove the stock down into this 200-week zone in the first place, so a Q3 update showing utilization re-accelerating kills this fast. Today's follow-through is on below-average relative volume (0.67x) and the scan's OBV divergence reads 'bearish' (cumulative volume not fully confirming the price highs yet) -- this is one good quarter, not yet a confirmed trend, so size is base risk only, not conviction. Current ratio of 0.8x is a liquidity watch line (though structurally normal for this business's float model).
proposal.variant_perception: CONSENSUS: analyst mean target is $437.81, just 0.8% above spot -- the Street is essentially neutral, still anchored to caution from last year's guidance-cut shock. MY VIEW: a ~30% EPS beat plus a genuine full-year guide raise (to $19.50-$20.00 from '>$18.25') plus resumed buyback execution is stronger evidence of durable medical-cost stabilization than the market's still-neutral positioning implies. MECHANISM: sell-side models were still built on conservative post-guidance-cut utilization assumptions; the beat's magnitude shows the reset working faster than modeled, and target/estimate revisions should catch up over the next 1-4 weeks as analysts update post-print -- that catch-up is the repricing mechanism, not multiple expansion alone. RESOLUTION: analyst estimate and price-target revisions over the next 2-3 weeks, and the Q3 2026 print (~mid-October) as the second-quarter confirmation the market will demand before fully re-rating.

thesis_invalidators.invalidating_print: A subsequent medical-cost-ratio miss, a Q3 pre-announcement, or any management commentary showing utilization trending worse than the 'returning to form' language from the Q2 call would kill this thesis outright.
thesis_invalidators.invalidating_structure: A decisive daily close back below the 200-week moving average (~$437.56) on rising volume, or a close below the 50-DMA, would show the reversal has failed.
thesis_invalidators.time_box: If UNH has not sustained a close above $460 (continuation toward the old 52-week-high zone) within 30 trading days of entry, exit and rotate -- the post-earnings gap needs volume-confirmed continuation, not just a one-day pop.
